name: Usage and metering
description: Events, data sources and billable metrics.
takeaways: Events cannot be edited or deleted
Visual builder to SQL builder is one way

cards.title: Usage event
cards.body: A report of one customer's usage at one point in time. What it reports is up to you: one action, a count over a minute, seats at noon, a file size.
cards.example: 14 API calls by customer c01 at 09:15.

cards.title: Collection and schema
cards.body: A collection is a named set of events with one data schema and one API slug. Two root fields are required: customer_id (String) and timestamp (DateTime64). Data fields hold the details.
cards.example: Collection api_calls with data.region and data.size_kb.

cards.title: Four ways in
cards.body: CSV file (one bad row means nothing is stored), one event manually, the collection's API endpoint with an API key, or S3 ingestion.

cards.title: Data field types
cards.body: String, Int64, Float64, Date32, DateTime64, UUID, Bool. Fields can be added later but not removed, renamed or retyped.

cards.title: Connector
cards.body: Instead of sending events, Zenskar can read usage from your systems through a connector such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake or BigQuery.
cards.example: The api_calls table in your warehouse.

cards.title: Synced vs remote
cards.body: A synced source is copied on a schedule (sync frequency and cursor columns keep it current). A remote source is queried in place.
cards.example: Redshift as a remote source queried from the SQL builder.

cards.title: S3 ingestion
cards.body: CSV files in a per-collection folder of your S3 bucket are read as they arrive. Webhooks report ingestion.completed and ingestion.failed.

cards.title: Four steps
cards.body: A metric filters rows, matches each row to a customer, keeps the rows of the period, then aggregates.
cards.example: 12,000 API calls for one customer in October.

cards.title: Visual builder
cards.body: Pick a table, filters, customer column, date column and one calculation type: count, sum, maximum, average, minimum or unique count. Count is the default.
cards.example: Sum of size_kb where region = eu-west.

cards.title: SQL builder
cards.body: Write a query. One value is the metric. With several columns, name the number quantity and the rest become dimensions (for dimensional pricing). Tables are named raw_metric_ plus the API slug.
cards.example: SELECT COUNT(*) AS quantity FROM raw_metric_api_calls WHERE customer_id = {{customer.external_id}}

cards.title: SQL variables
cards.body: Zenskar fills in customer, contract, product and period values, including custom attributes: {{start_date}}, {{end_date}}, {{customer.custom_attributes.key}}.

edgeCases: Immutable events. Usage events cannot be edited or deleted and collections cannot be deleted. Corrections follow the correct historical usage guide.
Schema is permanent. A data field cannot be removed, renamed or retyped, and the API slug never changes.
CSV is all or nothing. If one row fails the schema check, none are stored.
One-way move. A visual-builder metric moved to the SQL builder cannot return.
Missing quantity column. A multi-column query without a column named quantity gives 0 or fails.
No value vs 0. A sum over a month with no events gives no value; a count gives 0. This can change the charge, so wrap sums in COALESCE.
Deleting a metric. It is allowed even when a pricing preset uses it, and can affect contracts and invoices.
Customer matching. By default customer_id is matched to the customer external ID or Zenskar ID. Mismatched IDs mean unbilled usage.
BigQuery. May need fully qualified table names.

api.note: Documented endpoint for sending events: https://api.zenskar.com/usage/{api_slug}, with an API key in the x-api-key header, carrying one event or a list. The API reference also lists an update operation for usage events, while the product guide says events cannot be edited. Confirm behaviour with an SME before relying on it.

quiz.question: Which two root fields does every usage event need?
quiz.explanation: These are the only root fields Zenskar requires at the top level.

quiz.question: A CSV has 500 rows and one fails the schema check. What happens?
options: The bad row is skipped silently
quiz.explanation: Zenskar validates every row first and stores none if one fails.

quiz.question: You find a wrong usage event. Can you edit it in the product?
options: No, events cannot be edited or deleted
quiz.explanation: Use the historical usage correction approach instead.

quiz.question: A SQL builder query returns region and quantity columns. What does the metric give?
quiz.explanation: Other columns become dimensions, which dimensional pricing uses.

quiz.question: A sum over a month with no events returns…
options: No value, unlike count which returns 0
quiz.explanation: No value and 0 can lead to different charges.

qa.question: Usage event definition vs usage event?
qa.answer: A definition (collection, created at /rawmetrics) is the schema and API slug. A usage event is one record sent to /usage/{api_slug}.

qa.question: Usage events vs aggregates?
qa.answer: Events are individual timestamped records. Aggregates are pre-summarized values, which can be used directly without aggregation.

qa.question: Usage event vs billable metric?
qa.answer: The event is raw data. The billable metric turns events into the billable quantity for a customer and period.

qa.question: Synced vs remote data source?
qa.answer: Synced is copied on a schedule. Remote is queried in place.

qa.question: Visual builder vs SQL builder?
qa.answer: Visual builder offers one calculation on filtered rows. SQL builder allows any query and multi-column results, but you cannot move back to visual.

qa.question: Count vs unique count?
qa.answer: Count counts rows. Unique count counts distinct values of a chosen column, so retried events with the same ID count once.

qa.question: Sum vs maximum?
qa.answer: Sum adds values over the period; maximum keeps the peak, useful for peak concurrent seats.

qa.question: CSV vs API vs S3 ingestion?
qa.answer: CSV is a one-off upload (all or nothing). API is real time per event. S3 reads CSV files as they land in a per-collection folder.

qa.question: Bill per API call?
qa.answer: Count of events in the period.

qa.question: Bill the busiest hour of seats used?
qa.answer: Maximum.

qa.question: Bill distinct active users?
qa.answer: Unique count on the user column.

qa.question: Usage already sits in Snowflake?
qa.answer: Connect it as a data source and read from it instead of re-sending events.

qa.question: Protect against retried requests?
qa.answer: Include an event ID field in data and use unique count or COUNT(DISTINCT). Zenskar stores events as they arrive, so plain count would include both.

qa.question: Different price per region?
qa.answer: Return quantity plus a region dimension from SQL and use dimensional pricing.

qa.question: A usage event is wrong. Can I edit or delete it?
qa.answer: Not in the product. Events and collections cannot be edited or deleted; use the historical usage correction guide.

qa.question: Can I rename or remove a data field?
qa.answer: No. Fields can be added later but not removed, renamed or retyped, and the API slug never changes.

qa.question: One CSV row fails validation?
qa.answer: No rows are stored.

qa.question: A month has no events: sum or count?
qa.answer: Sum gives no value while count gives 0, which can change the charge. Wrap sums in COALESCE.

qa.question: The query returns several columns but no quantity?
qa.answer: The metric gives 0 or fails. Name the numeric column quantity.

qa.question: customer_id does not match any customer?
qa.answer: The usage is not attributed or billed. Check that it matches the external ID or Zenskar ID.

qa.question: Can I delete a metric a price uses?
qa.answer: It is allowed and can affect contracts and invoices.

qa.question: Which fields must every event have?
qa.answer: customer_id (String) and timestamp (DateTime64), plus your own fields under data.

qa.question: How does a metric know the billing period?
qa.answer: SQL variables {{start_date}} and {{end_date}} are filled in for the period.

qa.question: How do I know S3 ingestion finished?
qa.answer: Webhooks ingestion.completed and ingestion.failed report each file.
